note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 4ef90497c6). Section 4: "It is noted that the normal BGP procedures MUST be followed when the TCP session terminates due to the sending or receiving of a BGP NOTIFICATION message." The earlier finding (GR compared against "notification" while the reactor only ever sent "session closed" or "connection lost") is fixed: reactor/peer_close.go::sessionCloseFor returns rpc.ReasonNotification whenever notificationExchanged is set, and gr.go handleStructuredState and handleStateEvent compare against that constant. TestPeerCloseNamesTheNotificationTheNeighborSent drives a running Peer that receives a Cease and asserts the observer sees rpc.ReasonNotification with Event 25; TestRFC4724NotificationCloseRetainsNothing feeds that reason to the production GR callbacks and asserts no purge-stale, retain-routes or mark-stale dispatch, so the RIB clears the Adj-RIB-In on DOWN (rib.go, retainedPeers unset). Negatives TestPeerCloseNamesTheTransportLoss (TCP drop, rpc.ReasonTCPFailure) and TestRFC4724TransportCloseRetains (three-command sequence for TCPFailure and LocalClose) are genuine contrasts. The sending half has no tagged end-to-end unit: it rests on incrNotificationSent setting notificationExchanged (asserted by an untagged unit in reactor/peer_stats_test.go) and on the notified=true rows of untagged TestSessionCloseForCoversEveryCause. The older tagged gr_state_test.go units inject wasNotification and prove only the state-machine branch. Not covered: the text-event path handleStateEvent, which external GR plugins take.
